news.title: ‘Shock horror’ – Argentina reveal stance on Gianni Infantino after World Cup controversy
news.lede: Argentina have gone against the status quo amid increasing calls for Infantino to resign after his failed plans to launch the controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE). UEFA have reiterated their threat of boycotting the World Cup given that the 56-year-old acknowledged the mistakes with FFE, but is still in post. They have 'lost confidence' in his presidency, whilst the Jordanian FA president Prince Ali bin Al Hussein made an accusation of 'blackmail' over endorsement of his re-election. However, Infantino has received backing from the AFA, who released a statement to explain that he should continue as president.

news.title: Players union slams FIFA 'abuse of power' as UEFA doubles down on boycott
news.lede: Mexico and Argentina's football associations are the latest to have thrown their support behind embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino despite his botched World Cup stake sale plans. On Wednesday night, Infantino was also given the "full support" of FIFA's management board in a statement despite being forced to abandon his plan to sell stakes in a company to run the World Cup to private investors. Elsewhere African football's governing body, CAF - a long-time supporter of Infantino - "unanimously reconfirmed" its support for the president and went as far as thanking him "for his contribution to African football" as well as endorsing the statement released by FIFA. Mexico and Argentina 's football associations have now also thrown their support behind Infantino.

news.title: Mexico, Argentina back Infantino as FIFA fight rages on
news.lede: No clear candidate to stand against Infantino in the election in March has yet emerged, however, and the Swiss administrator still enjoys considerable support. The football associations of Mexico and Argentina have thrown their support behind FIFA president Gianni Infantino, as the world football chief faces a fierce backlash over a now-abandoned proposal to sell off some of the commercial rights to the World Cup. The Mexican Football Federation (FMF), co-host of the recently concluded World Cup, has broken ranks with its own regional confederation by backing Infantino after CONCACAF called for a “comprehensive reckoning” with his presidency. On Aug 6, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) unanimously backed Infantino’s leadership, but European football’s governing body UEFA said it remained committed to boycotting the World Cup and other FIFA competitions.

news.title: ‘My plan A, B and C is Scaloni’: Tapia backs World Cup-winning coach to stay
news.lede: Argentine Football Association (AFA) president Claudio Tapia has reaffirmed his full support for national team coach Lionel Scaloni, insisting the World Cup-winning manager remains his only choice to lead the Albiceleste despite ongoing speculation over his future. Speaking to TyC Sports, Tapia said he hopes Scaloni will extend his contract, stressing that the 48-year-old coach is his "plan A, B and C" for the Argentina job. "I love Gringo very much. He went through some tough times here," Tapia said, referring to Scaloni by his nickname.

news.title: Bayern Munich legend Thomas Müller thinks MLS has gained prestige because of the World Cup
news.lede: In his personal monthly newspaper, Bayern Munich legend Thomas Müller spoke about the upcoming MLS season and what he’s been focused on these last few weeks. In it, he included hope that the World Cup and an influx of new star players has helped MLS raise its profile on the global stage. “I’m really burning to be on the pitch for 90 minutes regularly and help my lads with everything I’ve got,” wrote Müller. “We have six games in three weeks.

news.title: Infantino gets lifeline with African support, UEFA maintains World Cup boycott threat
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino received a lifeline on Thursday when the Confederation of African Football (CAF) unanimously backed his leadership, but the support from one of the largest voting blocs is unlikely to end scrutiny on how the sport is governed globally. The endorsement from CAF, whose 54 member associations account for more than a quarter of FIFA's 211 members, handed Infantino a much needed boost as he seeks a fourth term in office. However, it does little to quell wider unrest within the global governing body, where opposition has intensified following his failed attempt to open the World Cup to private equity investment. "We are committed to continue working together with FIFA, its member associations, other football Confederations and stakeholders to safeguard and adhere to governance, due process, and transparency," CAF President Patrice Motsepe said in a statement.

news.title: 'World football split in two': FIFA bows its head vs. sharp UEFA... "World Cup boycott remains valid" despite Infantino's apology
news.lede: Despite the Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) withdrawing its plan to sell World Cup shares and an apology from FIFA President Gianni Infantino (56), UEFA has maintained its stance on boycotting major tournaments. According to international media reports, including the UK's BBC on the 7th, UEFA stated, "We require assurance that the plan to sell tournament shares has been withdrawn and that no similar attempts will be made in the future." It further added, "We have already lost trust in In Pan-ti-no (Chairman)'s leadership, and our position remains valid." This conflict originated from In Pan-ti-no (Chairman)'s plan to establish a new corporation, 'FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE),' aiming to sell shares of major tournaments such as the men's and women's World Cups to private investors.
